title: Sakura Finetek Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI Tissue Processor - Analyzer Will Not Power On or Complete Initialization
description: Troubleshoots no-power, incomplete startup, initialization failures, external power problems, connection issues, and conditions preventing the tissue processor from becoming ready.

steps.title: 1. Protect Specimens and Maintain Workflow Continuity
steps.instructions: Determine whether specimens are currently inside the processor or whether an active processing cycle was interrupted. If specimen integrity could be affected, immediately involve laboratory staff so specimens can be managed according to laboratory procedures. Do not repeatedly cycle power on equipment containing specimens without considering the effect on the active process. Expected outcome: Specimens are protected, laboratory staff understand the equipment status, and troubleshooting can proceed safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask staff whether the Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI is completely unresponsive, powers on but stops during initialization, displays a message, repeatedly restarts, or remains in a not-ready condition. Record any displayed message exactly before resetting or restarting the unit. Expected outcome: The failure point is clearly identified and any useful displayed information is preserved.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Unsafe Conditions
steps.instructions: Check for liquid leakage, chemical odor beyond normal operating conditions, smoke, overheating, damaged wiring, evidence of fluid intrusion, or other physical damage. If any unsafe condition is present, disconnect the equipment from use when safe to do so and stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: No condition is present that makes continued external troubleshooting unsafe. If one is found, remove the processor from service and escalate.

steps.title: 4. Verify AC Power
steps.instructions: Confirm that the processor is connected securely to its intended power source. Inspect the accessible power cord, plug, strain relief, and external connection for damage or looseness. Verify the outlet using an appropriate electrical test method or known-good equipment when permitted by facility policy. Check whether a facility breaker, emergency-power condition, switched outlet, or local power interruption explains the complaint. Expected outcome: Stable facility power is available and the external power connection is secure. If correcting the power source restores normal startup, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Accessible Power Controls
steps.instructions: Verify that accessible main power controls are in the proper operating position and have not been inadvertently switched off. Do not bypass interlocks, protective devices, or internal power circuitry. Expected outcome: External power controls are correctly positioned and the unit responds normally.

steps.title: 6. Inspect External Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible communication, peripheral, and power connections for loose connectors, damage, pin deformation, contamination, or tension on cables. Reseat only connections intended for normal external access. Expected outcome: Required external connections are secure and undamaged. If initialization completes after correcting a loose connection, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Allow a Normal Initialization Attempt
steps.instructions: If no unsafe condition is present and laboratory staff confirm that restarting will not jeopardize specimens, perform one controlled restart using the normal operating controls. Observe where startup stops and whether the same condition repeats. Expected outcome: The Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI completes initialization and reaches its normal ready state. If it does, troubleshooting can stop after verifying normal operation.

steps.title: 8. Evaluate Environmental and Utility Conditions
steps.instructions: Confirm that the unit is not being affected by obvious environmental problems such as excessive heat, blocked external ventilation, nearby fluid spills, unstable electrical service, or recent facility work. If the problem began after a power event, relocation, maintenance activity, or facility utility change, document that relationship. Expected outcome: No external environmental or utility condition is preventing initialization.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After a successful correction, verify that the system completes startup without abnormal messages, reaches its expected ready condition, and that accessible controls and indicators operate normally. Coordinate with laboratory staff before releasing the processor for specimen processing. Expected outcome: The processor initializes normally and is ready for clinical laboratory use. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI would not complete initialization after being powered on.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the processor connected to an outlet that was not supplying normal facility power.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the processor to a verified power source, confirmed successful initialization and normal ready status, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the unit was completely unresponsive or partially initialized
Whether specimens were inside the processor
Recent power interruption or facility work

title: Sakura Finetek Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI Tissue Processor - Barcode, LIS, or Network Communication Fails
description: Troubleshoots configured barcode, network, data-interface, and laboratory-system communication failures using external connectivity and configuration checks first.

steps.title: 1. Protect Specimen Identification and Traceability
steps.instructions: If the communication problem affects specimen identification, tracking, or documentation, do not rely on incomplete electronic information. Laboratory staff should use an approved alternate workflow until reliable identification and communication are restored. Expected outcome: Specimen identity and traceability are preserved during troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Communication Path Has Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves barcode reading, network connectivity, an LIS or middleware interface, data transfer, or another configured communication function. Do not assume all communication functions share the same cause. Expected outcome: The failed portion of the communication path is isolated.

steps.title: 3. Record Messages and Connection Status
steps.instructions: Capture any displayed communication message and note network or interface status indicators available through normal user-accessible screens. Expected outcome: The current communication state is documented before changes are made.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Network Connections
steps.instructions: If the processor uses a wired network connection, inspect the accessible network cable and connectors for looseness, damage, broken retention tabs, or obvious cable stress. Reseat the connection if appropriate. Expected outcome: The physical network connection is secure. If communication returns, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Test With a Known-Good Cable or Port When Authorized
steps.instructions: Use a known-good compatible network cable or coordinate with IT to verify the connected network port. Do not move the processor to an unapproved network or arbitrarily change network settings. Expected outcome: The cable and facility network connection are either verified or identified as the source of the problem.

steps.title: 6. Check Barcode Hardware When Applicable
steps.instructions: If the complaint involves barcode recognition, inspect the accessible scanner or reader for contamination, cable problems, physical damage, or poor positioning. Use a known-good representative barcode approved by the laboratory to determine whether the problem is specific to one label. Expected outcome: The reader successfully recognizes a valid barcode, or the failure is shown to affect the reader/interface rather than one label.

steps.title: 7. Confirm Configuration Has Not Recently Changed
steps.instructions: Coordinate with laboratory IT or the appropriate support group to determine whether network, LIS, middleware, server, or interface changes occurred before the failure. Do not alter IP addresses, interface parameters, or other managed settings without authorization. Expected outcome: Recent infrastructure or configuration changes are identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 8. Isolate Device Versus Infrastructure
steps.instructions: Determine whether other devices communicating with the same LIS, network segment, or interface are functioning normally. If multiple devices are affected, escalate to IT or the appropriate interface-support team rather than treating the processor as the only failure point. Expected outcome: The fault is narrowed to the Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI, an external connection, or shared infrastructure.

steps.title: 9. Verify End-to-End Communication
steps.instructions: After correction, confirm the complete intended path rather than relying solely on a connected indicator. Verify that representative data can be transmitted or received as appropriate to the configured workflow. Expected outcome: The intended barcode or communication function works end to end. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI was no longer communicating with the configured laboratory network interface.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network cable connection partially disconnected at the processor.
CCR.Resolution: The cable was reseated and inspected, end-to-end communication was verified with laboratory staff, and the processor was returned to normal service.

helpfulDetails: Barcode, network, or LIS function affected

title: Sakura Finetek Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI Tissue Processor - Calibration Fails or Will Not Complete
description: Troubleshoots failed verification, calibration-related, sensor-check, or service test conditions without changing restricted calibration parameters or entering unauthorized service functions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Specimens and Remove the Processor From Active Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not perform calibration, verification, or service testing while specimens depend on the processor unless specifically permitted by approved procedures. Transfer pending work to another verified processing workflow when necessary. Expected outcome: No specimens are placed at risk during technical evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm What “Calibration” Means in the Reported Event
steps.instructions: Determine exactly what procedure failed. Laboratory staff may use “calibration” to describe a system check, verification routine, sensor test, startup check, or other maintenance function. Record the exact test name and displayed message without assuming a specific calibration procedure. Expected outcome: The actual failed procedure is identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Normal Startup and Ready Status
steps.instructions: Before troubleshooting a calibration-related complaint, confirm that the processor powers on normally and is not already reporting unrelated power, fluidics, temperature, pressure, reagent, or communication problems. Expected outcome: The processor is otherwise operational, or a more fundamental fault is identified that should be corrected first.

steps.title: 4. Check External Conditions Required for the Procedure
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible reagent containers, waste connections, processing components, covers, lids, and other external items required for normal operation. Confirm there are no obvious leaks, empty required supplies, incorrectly positioned components, or open covers affecting the test. Expected outcome: External prerequisites for the procedure are satisfied.

steps.title: 5. Confirm Correct Procedure Selection
steps.instructions: Have authorized laboratory or service personnel verify that the intended approved procedure is being selected and that required setup conditions are met. Do not access restricted service menus or change hidden calibration parameters. Expected outcome: The proper authorized procedure is being performed under the correct setup conditions.

steps.title: 6. Review Recent Maintenance or Changes
steps.instructions: Determine whether the failure began after reagent changes, cleaning, preventive maintenance, relocation, software work, component replacement, or a power interruption. Inspect any externally accessible item disturbed during that work. Expected outcome: A simple setup or connection problem related to recent activity is corrected, or recent changes are ruled out.

steps.title: 7. Repeat the Approved Check Once
steps.instructions: If all prerequisites are correct, no specimens are at risk, and the procedure is approved for Clinical Engineering use, repeat the verification or calibration-related check once. Do not repeatedly force a procedure that consistently fails. Expected outcome: The procedure completes successfully. If it does, continue to final functional verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Confirm the Failure Is Repeatable
steps.instructions: If the same failure recurs, document the exact point of failure and any associated system message. Avoid changing unrelated settings in an attempt to force a passing result. Expected outcome: A reproducible service condition is documented for escalation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: If the procedure succeeds after correcting an external condition, verify normal system readiness and confirm that no related warnings remain. Expected outcome: The processor completes the required check and is ready for normal operation.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that a required system verification would not complete successfully.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that an externally accessible processing component was not fully seated after routine cleaning.
CCR.Resolution: The component was correctly reseated, the approved verification completed successfully, normal system readiness was confirmed, and the processor was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact procedure or test that failed

title: Sakura Finetek Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI Tissue Processor - Clot, Bubble, or Sample-Volume Error Repeats
description: Troubleshoots repeated flow, air, volume, obstruction, or fluid-transfer conditions that may be described as clot, bubble, or sample-volume errors.

steps.title: 1. Protect Specimens
steps.instructions: If the repeated condition occurs during an active processing cycle, have laboratory personnel evaluate specimen status before additional test cycles or fluid movement are attempted. Expected outcome: Specimens are protected from repeated or incomplete processing conditions.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Actual Message and Context
steps.instructions: Record the exact message displayed by the processor. Determine whether “clot,” “bubble,” or “sample-volume” is staff terminology for a more general fluid-level, flow, air, pressure, or reagent-transfer problem. Note which stage and reagent were involved. Expected outcome: The true device-reported condition is identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Reagent Quantity and Container Setup
steps.instructions: Check that the appropriate reagent container is installed correctly and that its contents are consistent with laboratory operating requirements. Look for an empty, improperly filled, incorrectly positioned, or loosely connected container. Expected outcome: Reagent availability and container setup are correct.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Tubing and Connections
steps.instructions: Look for kinks, loose fittings, damaged tubing, pinched sections, poor container connections, or visible air entry at accessible interfaces. Do not dismantle internal fluid pathways. Expected outcome: External fluid connections are secure and free of obvious conditions that could introduce air or restrict flow.

steps.title: 5. Inspect for Residue or Obstruction
steps.instructions: Check routinely accessible fluid-contact and seating areas for tissue debris, paraffin, dried reagent, or other contamination that may affect normal fluid transfer. Clean only according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: Accessible areas are free of visible obstruction.

steps.title: 6. Check Waste and Drain Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that accessible waste containers and drainage connections are installed correctly and are not creating an obvious restriction. Expected outcome: Waste handling is not interfering with fluid movement.

steps.title: 7. Determine Whether the Error Follows One Position
steps.instructions: Review whether the repeated condition occurs with one specific reagent position or across multiple positions. If limited to one position, inspect its container and accessible connections carefully and compare them with a normally functioning position. Expected outcome: The failure either follows an external reagent setup or is shown to be processor-related.

steps.title: 8. Run an Approved Fluidics Verification
steps.instructions: With specimens removed from risk, perform an approved operational check of the affected function if authorized. Do not repeatedly run cycles simply to see whether the fault returns. Expected outcome: The fluidics function completes normally without recurring air, flow, or volume-related warnings.

steps.title: 9. Confirm Stable Operation
steps.instructions: Verify that the problem does not recur during the approved check and that no leakage, unusual sounds, or secondary fluidics warnings are present. Expected outcome: Fluid movement is stable and normal. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported a repeated fluid-volume-related warning during processing.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose accessible connection at the affected reagent container that could allow inconsistent fluid transfer.
CCR.Resolution: The connection was secured, the external fluid path was inspected, approved operation completed without recurrence, and the processor was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the error repeats in one position

title: Sakura Finetek Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI Tissue Processor - Probe, Pipettor, or Aspiration Error Occurs
description: Troubleshoots reagent-transfer, aspiration, fluid-movement, tubing, container, connection, and obstruction conditions associated with a reported probe, pipettor, or aspiration-type error.

steps.title: 1. Protect Specimens and Stop Unreliable Processing
steps.instructions: If an aspiration or fluid-transfer condition occurs during tissue processing, have laboratory personnel assess the specimens and processing stage before further troubleshooting. Do not continue processing when reagent transfer is unreliable. Expected outcome: Specimens are protected and the processor is not relied upon for uncertain fluid movement.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Error
steps.instructions: Capture the exact message displayed by the Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI rather than relying only on the general description “probe,” “pipettor,” or “aspiration error.” Determine which reagent or stage was active when the problem occurred. Expected outcome: The actual fluid-transfer complaint and affected portion of the cycle are identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Reagent Availability
steps.instructions: Confirm that the required reagent container is present and contains sufficient usable reagent according to laboratory procedures. Check for an incorrectly positioned or disconnected container. Expected outcome: The affected reagent source is present and correctly installed.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Accessible Fluid Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible tubing, caps, fittings, and container interfaces for loose connections, kinks, compression, leakage, damage, or obvious blockage. Do not disassemble internal valves, pumps, or manifolds. Expected outcome: The external reagent path is properly connected and unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Check Waste and Venting Conditions
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible waste containers and associated connections for improper installation, overfill conditions, kinks, or other obvious conditions that could interfere with normal fluid transfer. Verify that external openings or connections intended to remain unobstructed are not blocked. Expected outcome: Waste and accessible venting arrangements are normal.

steps.title: 6. Look for Residue or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect routinely accessible areas associated with reagent transfer for paraffin, tissue debris, dried reagent, or other residue that could interfere with normal operation. Clean only areas approved for routine access. Expected outcome: No external residue is interfering with fluid movement.

steps.title: 7. Compare the Affected Reagent Position
steps.instructions: If the problem appears limited to one reagent position, compare its container, connection, and routing with another correctly functioning position. Do not interchange incompatible reagents for testing. Expected outcome: A container or connection-specific problem is identified, or the fault remains associated with the processor.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Functional Check
steps.instructions: With patient specimens removed from risk, perform an approved operating or service check that exercises the relevant fluidics function if such a check is authorized and available. Do not manually energize internal pumps or valves. Expected outcome: Fluid transfer completes without the error. If it does, proceed to final verification and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 9. Verify Reliable Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the affected fluidics condition no longer recurs and that there are no leaks, abnormal sounds, or additional warnings. Expected outcome: Reagent transfer is reliable and the processor is suitable for return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported a repeated fluid aspiration error during tissue processing.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible reagent tubing connection partially kinked at the container interface.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing was correctly repositioned, the connection was inspected for damage, approved fluid-transfer operation was verified without recurrence, and the processor was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Processing stage when the error occurred

title: Sakura Finetek Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI Tissue Processor - Quality-Control Results Are Out of Range
description: Troubleshoots processing-quality concerns, verification failures, and inconsistent tissue-processing outcomes while separating equipment conditions from reagent, protocol, and specimen factors.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Specimens
steps.instructions: If laboratory staff report unacceptable processing quality, stop using the processor for additional patient specimens until the scope of the issue is understood. Affected specimens must be managed by qualified laboratory personnel. Expected outcome: Additional specimens are not exposed to a potentially unreliable processing condition.

steps.title: 2. Define the Reported Quality Problem
steps.instructions: Ask laboratory staff what was observed and whether the issue involves one specimen, one batch, multiple runs, or all specimens processed on the unit. Determine when the problem began and whether a specific processing program, reagent set, or workflow is involved. Expected outcome: The pattern of the processing-quality complaint is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Review Device Status and Event Information
steps.instructions: Check the processor for active or recent warnings, incomplete cycles, power interruptions, fluidics warnings, temperature-related conditions, or other operational abnormalities associated with the affected run. Do not infer a hardware failure solely from the tissue result. Expected outcome: Any equipment-generated indication relevant to the affected cycle is identified.

steps.title: 4. Verify Reagent Setup
steps.instructions: With laboratory staff, confirm that required reagents were present, correctly positioned, suitable for use under laboratory procedures, and represented correctly in the system. Look for obvious container, connection, leakage, or inventory discrepancies. Expected outcome: The reagent setup is verified or an external reagent-related cause is identified.

steps.title: 5. Verify the Processing Program
steps.instructions: Have authorized laboratory staff confirm that the intended processing program was selected for the affected specimens and that no unauthorized settings or protocol changes occurred. Clinical Engineering should not independently alter clinical processing protocols. Expected outcome: The correct program was used, or a workflow/configuration discrepancy is identified.

steps.title: 6. Check for Facility or Environmental Events
steps.instructions: Determine whether the affected processing period coincided with a power interruption, relocation, temperature problem, utility issue, maintenance event, or other environmental change. Expected outcome: External facility conditions are either identified as a contributing factor or ruled out.

steps.title: 7. Compare With Previous and Other-System Results
steps.instructions: When available, ask laboratory staff whether similar specimens processed on another verified processor produced acceptable results and whether prior runs on this unit were normal. This helps distinguish a device-specific trend from specimen, reagent, or laboratory-process variation. Expected outcome: The comparison narrows the problem to the processor or identifies a broader workflow/reagent issue.

steps.title: 8. Perform Approved Operational Verification
steps.instructions: With the processor free of patient specimens, perform only approved functional checks appropriate to Clinical Engineering and the available manufacturer documentation. Do not use patient tissue as a technical test load. Expected outcome: The processor either demonstrates normal operation or reproduces an equipment-related abnormal condition.

steps.title: 9. Confirm Suitability Before Return to Service
steps.instructions: Return the processor to use only after the suspected cause has been corrected and laboratory personnel are satisfied that required quality verification has been successfully completed. Expected outcome: Processing quality and device operation have been appropriately verified. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported inconsistent tissue-processing quality from specimens processed on the Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering and laboratory staff found that the installed reagent configuration did not match the intended processing setup.
CCR.Resolution: Laboratory staff corrected the reagent configuration, Clinical Engineering verified normal processor operation, required laboratory quality checks were completed, and the unit was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Description of the observed processing problem
Number of affected specimens or runs
Laboratory acceptance before return to service

title: Sakura Finetek Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI Tissue Processor - Reagent Is Not Recognized or Inventory Is Incorrect
description: Troubleshoots reagent identification, container placement, inventory records, reagent status, connection issues, and discrepancies between physical reagents and displayed information.

steps.title: 1. Protect Specimens and Processing Integrity
steps.instructions: If a processing cycle is active or specimens are loaded, do not change reagent positions, containers, or processing configuration until laboratory staff determine that doing so is safe. Incorrect reagent selection can compromise specimen processing. Expected outcome: Specimens and the current processing workflow are protected before troubleshooting begins.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reagent Discrepancy
steps.instructions: Determine whether the processor is failing to recognize a reagent, showing the wrong reagent, displaying an incorrect volume or status, or reporting inventory that does not match what is physically installed. Record the exact displayed information. Expected outcome: The specific discrepancy between the physical reagent setup and system display is established.

steps.title: 3. Compare the Physical Reagent Setup With the Display
steps.instructions: With laboratory staff, compare the installed reagent containers and positions with the expected processor configuration. Do not assume a displayed inventory value is correct without checking the physical setup. Expected outcome: Physical reagent placement agrees with the intended configuration, or a placement discrepancy is identified.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Reagent Containers and Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible reagent containers, caps, tubing interfaces, fittings, and associated external connections for improper seating, loose connections, damage, leaks, kinks, or obvious contamination. Do not open internal fluid-control assemblies. Expected outcome: Reagent containers and accessible connections are correctly installed and free of obvious defects.

steps.title: 5. Verify Reagent Information Entered Into the System
steps.instructions: Have authorized laboratory personnel confirm that reagent identification, replacement status, and other user-managed inventory information have been entered correctly according to established laboratory procedures. Clinical Engineering should not alter laboratory processing protocols or reagent assignments without authorization. Expected outcome: System information accurately reflects the physical reagent configuration.

steps.title: 6. Check for Recent Reagent Changes
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint began after a reagent bottle was replaced, moved, refilled, exchanged, or reassigned. If so, inspect that change first for incorrect placement or incomplete setup. Expected outcome: Any discrepancy introduced during a recent reagent change is corrected. If the displayed inventory then matches the physical setup, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Position or Container When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If laboratory procedures permit, compare the affected reagent setup with another correctly recognized position or known-good compatible container. Do not interchange chemicals merely for troubleshooting unless laboratory staff confirm that it is appropriate. Expected outcome: The comparison helps distinguish an accessory/container problem from a processor-side recognition or inventory problem.

steps.title: 8. Check for Communication or Display Synchronization Issues
steps.instructions: If the physical setup is correct but displayed information remains inconsistent, verify that the user interface is responsive and that no broader startup, communication, or configuration problem is present. A controlled restart may be performed only if laboratory staff confirm specimens and processing will not be jeopardized. Expected outcome: The display and physical reagent configuration agree after correction or restart.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm that all affected reagents are represented correctly, the processor reaches the appropriate ready condition, no leak or fluidics warning is present, and laboratory staff agree that the reagent configuration is correct. Expected outcome: Reagent information is accurate and stable. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the reagent inventory displayed on the Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI did not match the installed reagent setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that a recently changed reagent container had been installed in the wrong assigned position.
CCR.Resolution: Laboratory staff corrected the reagent placement, the displayed inventory was verified against the physical setup, and normal ready status was confirmed.

title: Sakura Finetek Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI Tissue Processor - Result Is Delayed, Missing, or Inconsistent
description: Troubleshoots delayed, incomplete, or inconsistent tissue-processing outcomes by checking cycle status, reagents, workflow, configuration, utilities, and equipment operation.

steps.title: 1. Protect Specimens and Confirm Their Status
steps.instructions: Immediately determine whether patient specimens are still inside the processor, whether processing completed, and whether laboratory staff consider the specimens adequately preserved. Do not initiate another cycle or alter the current state until specimen status is understood. Expected outcome: Specimens are accounted for and protected while the processing delay or inconsistency is investigated.

steps.title: 2. Define What Was Delayed, Missing, or Inconsistent
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint refers to an unfinished processing cycle, unexpected processing time, missing cycle information, incomplete processing, inconsistent tissue quality, or a data/documentation issue. Record the exact staff complaint and displayed status. Expected outcome: The actual failure mode is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Review Cycle Status and Messages
steps.instructions: Check normal user-accessible history, status information, and displayed messages for evidence of a pause, alarm, power interruption, reagent-transfer problem, fluidics condition, or other event associated with the affected run. Expected outcome: Any event that explains the delay or incomplete process is identified.

steps.title: 4. Verify Power Continuity
steps.instructions: Ask whether a facility power interruption, generator transfer, unplugging event, breaker operation, or other electrical disturbance occurred during the affected processing period. Inspect the processor's external power connection. Expected outcome: Power disruption is identified as a possible cause or ruled out.

steps.title: 5. Verify Reagent Configuration
steps.instructions: With laboratory personnel, confirm that required reagents were available, correctly positioned, and appropriately represented in the system. Inspect external containers and connections for obvious setup problems or leakage. Expected outcome: The reagent configuration is correct or an external cause is identified.

steps.title: 6. Verify the Processing Program
steps.instructions: Have authorized laboratory staff confirm that the intended processing program was selected and that the expected workflow was used. Do not independently change clinical processing protocols as a troubleshooting experiment. Expected outcome: Program selection is confirmed or a workflow discrepancy explains the event.

steps.title: 7. Inspect External Fluidics Conditions
steps.instructions: Check accessible tubing, reagent connections, waste containers, and processing components for kinks, loose connections, improper seating, visible obstruction, or leakage. Expected outcome: External fluidics conditions are normal or a correctable problem is found.

steps.title: 8. Check for Pattern or Recurrence
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint occurred once, follows a particular program or reagent position, or has appeared across several processing runs. Compare with prior normal operation and, when available, another verified processor. Expected outcome: The event is identified as isolated or repeatable, helping separate workflow variation from a processor-related condition.

steps.title: 9. Perform Approved Functional Verification
steps.instructions: With patient specimens removed from risk, perform appropriate approved operational checks based on the reported failure. Verify normal startup, readiness, accessible fluidics behavior, and absence of recurring warnings. Expected outcome: The processor demonstrates reliable operation without reproducing the reported condition.

steps.title: 10. Confirm Laboratory Acceptance Before Return to Service
steps.instructions: If the problem involved actual tissue-processing quality, laboratory personnel must complete whatever specimen-quality or workflow verification is required before normal clinical use resumes. Clinical Engineering verification of equipment operation does not replace laboratory acceptance of processing quality. Expected outcome: Equipment operation is verified and the laboratory accepts the processor for clinical workflow. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that a tissue-processing cycle took longer than expected and did not progress normally.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an improperly seated external reagent connection associated with the affected processing setup.
CCR.Resolution: The connection was correctly secured, approved processor operation was verified without further faults, laboratory staff confirmed the processing setup, and the unit was returned to service.

helpfulDetails: Cycle stage when the problem occurred

title: Sakura Finetek Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI Tissue Processor - Sample, Rack, or Carrier Is Not Detected
description: Troubleshoots tissue-container, basket, carrier, loading, positioning, or detection conditions that prevent the processor from recognizing a properly loaded processing setup.

steps.title: 1. Protect Specimens Before Troubleshooting
steps.instructions: If tissue specimens are involved, have laboratory staff secure them according to laboratory handling procedures before manipulating baskets, containers, or processor loading areas. Do not repeatedly start processing attempts while specimen location or loading status is uncertain. Expected outcome: Specimens remain accounted for and protected while the detection problem is investigated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm What Is Actually Not Being Detected
steps.instructions: Determine what staff mean by “sample, rack, or carrier not detected.” On a tissue processor, the complaint may involve a specimen basket, processing container, loading position, retort-related readiness condition, or another component required before processing can begin. Record the exact displayed message if one is present. Expected outcome: The specific item or loading condition associated with the complaint is identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Basket or Carrier Externally
steps.instructions: Check the applicable basket, carrier, lid, container, or other removable processing component for damage, deformation, contamination, incorrect assembly, or an object preventing normal seating. Do not modify the component to force acceptance. Expected outcome: The removable component is intact, clean enough for normal engagement, and correctly assembled.

steps.title: 4. Verify Correct Positioning
steps.instructions: Have qualified laboratory staff confirm that the basket or carrier is installed in the intended orientation and fully seated. Look for obvious obstructions, tissue debris, paraffin, residue, or other material preventing complete positioning. Expected outcome: The component sits fully and correctly in its intended position. If proper seating restores detection, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Detection Areas
steps.instructions: With the processor in a safe condition, visually inspect accessible areas associated with component detection for contamination, obstruction, or damage. Clean only external or routinely accessible surfaces using approved laboratory/device procedures. Do not disassemble sensors or internal mechanisms. Expected outcome: Accessible detection surfaces are unobstructed and undamaged.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Component
steps.instructions: If another compatible basket, carrier, or removable component is available and laboratory workflow allows, substitute a known-good item. If the known-good component is detected normally, inspect the original accessory more closely and remove it from use if damaged. Expected outcome: The comparison identifies whether the condition follows the removable component or remains with the processor.

steps.title: 7. Check Related Covers, Lids, and Accessible Interlocks
steps.instructions: Confirm that accessible covers, lids, and doors associated with normal processing are fully closed and correctly positioned. Do not defeat or bypass safety interlocks. Expected outcome: All required external closures are properly engaged and the processor recognizes the loading condition.

steps.title: 8. Restart Only if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If no specimens are at risk and laboratory staff approve, perform a normal restart to clear a temporary state or communication condition. Do not repeatedly restart the system if the same detection failure returns. Expected outcome: The system initializes normally and detects the correctly installed component. If so, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm that the processor consistently recognizes the basket, carrier, or applicable loading condition and reaches the expected ready state without requiring force or repeated repositioning. Expected outcome: The component is reliably detected and the processor is ready for normal use.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the processor would not recognize the loaded tissue basket.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found residue preventing the removable basket assembly from seating completely.
CCR.Resolution: The accessible seating area was cleaned according to approved procedures, the basket was reinstalled, reliable detection was verified, and the processor was returned to service.

title: Sakura Finetek Tissue-Tek VIP 6 AI Tissue Processor - Wash, Waste, or Fluidics System Fault Occurs
description: Troubleshoots reagent-transfer, waste, drainage, tubing, container, leakage, and external fluidics conditions that prevent normal tissue processing.

steps.title: 1. Protect Specimens and Control Chemical Hazards
steps.instructions: If specimens are being processed, involve laboratory staff immediately to protect them. If liquid is leaking, follow facility chemical-safety procedures and keep personnel away from the spill as appropriate. Do not continue operating equipment with uncontrolled leakage. Expected outcome: Specimens and personnel are protected before fluidics troubleshooting begins.

steps.title: 2. Record the Exact Fault
steps.instructions: Capture the complete displayed fluidics, waste, or wash-related message and identify when it occurred in the processing cycle. Determine whether the processor stopped, paused, or continued operating. Expected outcome: The specific fluidics condition and point of failure are known.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for External Leakage
steps.instructions: Visually inspect around the processor, reagent containers, accessible tubing, fittings, and waste containers for wetness, dripping, pooling, damaged containers, or chemical residue. If significant leakage is present, remove the processor from service. Expected outcome: No uncontrolled leak is present. Any leak discovered is contained and appropriately escalated.

steps.title: 4. Verify Reagent and Waste Containers
steps.instructions: Confirm that required reagent and waste containers are present, correctly positioned, properly connected, and not obviously overfilled, empty, damaged, or misidentified. Expected outcome: Containers are correctly installed and suitable for operation.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Tubing and Fittings
steps.instructions: Check external or routinely accessible tubing for kinks, compression, loose connections, visible obstruction, cracking, or improper routing. Do not open internal fluid manifolds or valve assemblies. Expected outcome: Accessible fluid paths are intact and unrestricted.

steps.title: 6. Check for External Obstructions
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible drain, container, lid, and connection areas for paraffin, tissue debris, dried reagent, or other residue that may interfere with flow. Clean only according to approved device and laboratory procedures. Expected outcome: Accessible fluid pathways and interfaces are free of visible obstruction.

steps.title: 7. Verify Covers and Components Are Properly Positioned
steps.instructions: Ensure that applicable lids, covers, containers, and removable processing components are fully installed. A component that is not seated correctly can cause a fluidics or safety condition. Expected outcome: All externally accessible components are correctly positioned.

steps.title: 8. Perform an Approved Fluidics Check
steps.instructions: With specimens removed from risk and only if safe to proceed, perform an approved check of the affected fluidics function. Observe for leakage, abnormal sound, failure to transfer fluid, or recurrence of the message. Expected outcome: Fluid movement completes normally without leakage or warnings. If so, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm stable ready status and normal operation of the affected fluidics pathway before releasing the processor. Expected outcome: The system completes the applicable fluidics function normally and is safe to return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported a fluidics fault and failure to complete the expected reagent-transfer portion of the processing cycle.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible waste connection improperly seated.
CCR.Resolution: The waste connection was correctly secured, the surrounding area was inspected for leakage, approved fluidics operation was verified, and the processor was returned to service.
